To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the geometric fitting of a circle/sphere/ ellipse/ hyperbola/par-abola is based on the coordinate descriptions of the corresponding points on the geometric feature to the given points, and that these are based on the nonparametric fitting of the orthogonal distance between the two points.

we have proposed simple and robust non-parametric algorithms for the geometric fitting of a circle, sphere, hyperbola and parabola, and we have proposed a new method for the geometric fitting ellipse that is based on the coordinate transformation of a circle to an ellipse.
the proposed nonparametric algorithms provide robust solutions to the geometric fitting problem of circle/sphere, ellipse, hyperbole and parabola.

the geometric fitting of a geometric feature is the least-squares fitting of the geometric feature in the sense that the error-of-fit is measured by the orthogonal distances from the given data points to the geometric features.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed nonparametric fitting algorithms are very simple and robust, which are based on the simple coordinate description of the fitting feature for the given points, and are applicable to all kinds of data, i.e., the data are not required to be ordered, or the data may be noisy, or the data are not necessarily in a small range of the fitting feature.
we have developed a new method for fitting geometric shapes, which is based on the coordinate representation of the point on the shape corresponding to the given point.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the least-squares orthogonal distance fitting of circle, ellipse, and sphere is equivalent to the least-squares fitting in the coordinate system of the corresponding geometric feature.
the geometric fitting of these five basic geometric features can be solved in the same way.
the orthogonal distances fitting is the most robust and accurate fitting method.
